coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No Montenegro-specific rule or product found; results were Croatian. Only context: RSE reports about 35,000 people working without a contract. Nothing new beyond the general employer-registration duty. Unverified whether private employers have a simplified registration route.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No dedicated scrap-metal law. Dealers fall under waste traders and intermediaries: Law on Waste Management SL CG 34/24, a register kept by the ministry (registration within 30 days, fee 2 EUR, at least 2 staff, one manager with level V qualification, insurance policy, storage-site description), and a Rulebook on waste records and transport forms (SL CG 50/12). Candidate C1. No local software found.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Search found nothing on Montenegrin pawnshop or second-hand dealer rules or police record duties. Nothing usable; unverified.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: The AML law (ZSPNFT, consolidated through amendments 59/26 of 4 May 2026) is in force and exchange offices are obliged entities. Could not confirm from the current text whether gold buyers or jewellers are obliged entities. MONEYVAL 2025 follow-up mentions dealers in precious metals and stones. Candidate C6 (unverified).

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Montenegrin end-of-life-vehicle rule or permit register found; results were Serbian and Croatian. Falls under the waste trader and collector regime (see C1). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Law on Identification and Registration of Animals (SL RCG 48/07, amended 73/10, 40/11, 48/15). Sheep and goat holders keep a holding register and count on 1 March and 31 December, reporting to the Uprava between 1 March and 15 April and by 15 January (SL CG 33/14, amended 61/18). Pigs: ear tags within 45 days of birth, request within 7 days. Movement documents: passport for cattle, movement certificate for sheep and goats. Candidate C4. Nothing found on livestock traders or transporters specifically.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: New Law on Food Safety (SL CG 59/26). A government decree of 23 July 2026 sets hygiene flexibilities for very small producers of animal-origin foods in registered farm facilities, which must be entered in the Uprava's register, with an annual control plan. An older 2016 decree covers small slaughter up to 10 livestock units a week (whether still in force unconfirmed). Candidate C3. The full decree text could not be read (PDF unreadable via fetch).

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No mandatory apiary registration found. Beekeepers register as farm holdings to claim subsidies: 2,361 beekeepers with 102,576 hives in the farm register. Subsidy calls exist (seljak.me). Candidate C9, weak.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Authorised vet clinics must be in the register of veterinary organisations and services, and the Uprava supervises them. Could not find the Montenegrin rule on veterinary medicine records (results were Croatian). Candidate C8, unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Law on Waters (SL RCG 27/07, amended through 2018) governs. Water consent (vodna saglasnost) and permit (vodna dozvola) are issued at national or municipal level. Could not confirm permit steps, fees or pumping logs for private wells. Candidate C10, unverified.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Nothing Montenegro-specific on septic emptying duties or hauler licensing; results were Serbian, Bosnian and Croatian. Waste carriers and collectors sit in the waste register regime (see C1). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Pravilnik on technical requirements for regular servicing and safety control of lifts in use (2019, Ministry of Spatial Planning; current status unconfirmed). Pressure-equipment rulebook SL CG 89/17, amended 2026 under the Law on Technical Requirements for Products (53/11, 3/23, 39/26). Not opened. Candidate C5, unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Law on health safety of drinking water defines village systems (under 200 inhabitants). The Institute of Public Health monitors; individual supplies below 50 users or 10 m3 a day are excluded. Asbestos-cement pipes remain in all municipalities except Plužine and Petnjica. Village water-user association duties not found. Candidate C7, weak.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: New Law on Plant Protection Products adopted 27 April 2026 and promulgated 30 April 2026. It covers authorisation, placing on the market, use, registers and records, official controls and training of professional users. The 2026 monitoring programme counts 8 importers and 76 wholesale and retail outlets. Use records are kept on prescribed Form 1 and Form 2 under the older rulebook. Article text could not be fetched (file over 10 MB). Candidate C2.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Law on Employment Mediation (SL CG 24/19, amended 29/2025 and 3/2026). Agencies need a ministry licence: at least 3 staff, one with a higher degree and 2 years' experience, licence issued within 15 days. 2026 foreign-worker quota is 28,988 permits (21,668 employment, 2,320 seasonal, 5,000 reserve). Law on Foreigners amended 31 Dec 2025 (consolidated reference 3/2026). Candidate C11, related to K02.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No Montenegrin cemetery or funeral-licensing source found; this is municipal and communal. Only Croatian and Serbian results. Nothing usable.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: The Ministry of Public Administration keeps the NGO register under the 2011 NGO law (about 5,389 associations in Jan 2020, with a Jan 2025 active list on data.gov.me). Annual reporting and beneficial-owner duties for associations not confirmed. Nothing on halal or kosher supervision. Candidate C12, unverified.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi carriers are governed by the Law on Road Transport (SL CG 71/17, 67/19) plus municipal decisions (e.g. Kotor, whose taxi decision is under Constitutional Court review). Taxi duties map to K06. Nothing found on trucking or bus fleets.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Market traders: nothing beyond K06 (fiscalisation). Exchange offices are obliged entities under the AML law, and a 10,000 EUR cash-payment limit applies. No exchange-office software gap checked.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Small food producers: see C3. Driving schools: licensed by the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation (a 2025 decision for a Podgorica school, A1 category); no general duties found. Tattoo studios, childminders, nurseries and hunting outfitters were not reached for lack of budget.

The Health Insurance Fund contracts private pharmacies and runs its own information system and e-prescription (since 1 Mar 2018), which looks like a state system. Not checked: how contracted private clinics bill the Fund (e.g. the Fund's e-billing).

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Private pharmacies (about 124 to 172 under Fund contracts, per 2017-2018 reports) use the Fund-supplied pharmacy information system for e-prescriptions, so this is state-covered. Precursors and medicine importers not checked.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Searches returned only Serbian and Kosovo private-security laws. No Montenegrin law, register or reporting duty confirmed. Marked unverified.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: New Law on Construction of Objects (Sl. list 19/2025, in force 5 Mar 2025; amended July 2025) replaced the 2017 planning and construction law. Site notice, construction diary and contractor duties under it are unconfirmed. Mining and quarries not checked.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: More than 460 real estate agencies are registered. They have had to report cash transactions over EUR 10,000 since Dec 2023. Police Administration supervises them. IMF (May 2024) and Moneyval (Feb 2024) flagged weak preventive measures. No law on real estate intermediation exists. Notaries' AML status was not confirmed.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K01, K03, K04. No new search was spent here because these are already covered.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: The Directorate for Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Affairs keeps the register of food establishments. EU export approval of establishments is tied to the Chapter 12 accession benchmarks. No Montenegrin list of EU-approved establishments found. Timber not checked.

coverage.category: 31. Packaging waste producer responsibility: producers and importers of packaged goods
coverage.found: The Law on Waste Management (Sl. list CG 34/24, 92/24) puts producers and importers under an organised packaging system with an operator. Waste reports go to the Environment Agency by 31 March. A 2024 analysis says the packaging system was still being designed. A plastic-bag fee decree (105/24) exists. Current forms, thresholds and operators unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 32. Nautical tourism, yacht charter and marinas
coverage.found: Monstat reports 4,836 foreign pleasure vessels entering Montenegrin waters in 2025. Maritime safety law is Sl. list 62/13 with later amendments. No Montenegrin charter or nautical-tourism levy or reporting duty confirmed. Unverified.

coverage.category: 33. Wine producers: vineyard register, harvest and stock declarations
coverage.found: The Law on Wine (Sl. list 41/16) and a 2016 rulebook set a vineyard register (vineyard file and winery file), harvest declarations (izjava o berbi), and production and stock declarations. The Ministry of Agriculture runs it. A public list of legal-entity wine producers is on data.gov.me. Current deadlines, forms and whether filing is electronic are unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 34. Beneficial-owner register for companies
coverage.found: A rulebook on entering and updating data in the Register of Beneficial Owners (Sl. list 68/24, 19 Jul 2024) uses a tax-authority web application. Filing deadline was 30 days from entry into force. An April 2026 unija.com article says a new law was adopted in 2025, but this was not confirmed. Applies to all legal entities, which makes it generic.

coverage.category: 35. Renewable energy: customer-producers (prosumers) and small solar
coverage.found: New Energy Law adopted March 2025, and a renewables law defines the customer-producer. EPCG's Solari programme has connected more than 9,150 buildings. No small-business filing duty found.

coverage.category: 36. Agricultural holdings and subsidies
coverage.found: Search returned only Serbian and Republika Srpska material. No Montenegro-specific farm register or Agrobudget call found. The Montenegrin ministry or payments directorate sites were not opened.

coverage.category: 37. Tourism services: rent-a-car, travel agencies, tourist guides
coverage.found: The Law on Tourism and Hospitality (Sl. list 2/2018 with amendments) covers these. It has rent-a-car limits for vehicles hired with a driver and rules on who may be a guide. No new law found for 2026 and no reporting duty confirmed.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Nothing strong. Montenegro has almost no domestic grain trade: Monstat shows maize output of about 3,586 t in 2025 and grain purchases of only about EUR 10k in Q3 2025, so a grain-trader or miller niche is tiny. I found no grain-warehouse licensing law. Serbia has a public-warehouse and commodity-receipt system, Montenegro has none. Commodity reserves were only at feasibility-study stage (a 2022 study, per a July 2024 ministry reply), and I found no draft law. Coffee roasting and importing falls under the general food-business register, customs and VAT. I found no coffee-specific register or levy (I could not confirm whether an excise applies). The only recurring duties I found: (a) Fito register entry for importers, distributors and warehouse keepers of plants and plant products, with an ME Fito number; the 2016 phytosanitary report counted 602 holders, mostly fruit importers, seed-potato producers and warehouse operators, and entry is also a precondition for registering plant-origin food businesses; (b) monthly Monstat purchase and sales reports, required of firms with 2 or more employees that buy from individual farms. Both are small, state-run, and have no software competitor I could confirm. I could not read the Fito regulation text (FAOLEX PDF is binary), so duties, renewal cycle and fees are unchecked.

result.reason: The laws exist, but I could not confirm a recurring record-keeping duty that software could serve. Law on Food Safety (SL CG 59/26) was adopted 27 April 2026. A Hygiene Decree followed on 28 May 2026. A 23 July 2026 decree covers small quantities of animal-origin products, with derogations from hygiene rules for registered farm facilities. That decree is a relaxation, not a new burden. Its search summary says facilities must be in the central register, and the Uprava publishes the list. The PDF would not parse, so I could not read its record, HACCP, deadline or penalty rules. The 2016 small-slaughter decree was not confirmed. No Montenegrin HACCP software turned up; a regional app, FUDO, exists but has no evidenced Montenegrin presence. Facility count not found. Registration looks one-off and the buyers are tiny farms, so willingness to pay looks low.
